mascotLines: Firms can finally see what an employee costs per hour. I've always cost exactly one belly rub, flat rate, no negotiation.
Clients now have to say "yes, I actually reviewed this" before signing a tax return. I make that same face before agreeing to a bath.
You can print a proposal draft before anyone else sees it. I have never once let a treat leave the counter unsupervised either.
The Desktop app remembers you for 30 days straight. I remember exactly one thing for 30 days running: where the treats live.

items.text: Employee cost rate
items.desc: Firms can now set an hourly cost rate for each team member, right alongside billing rates — the first step toward seeing true job and client profitability instead of just billed revenue. Rate changes never retroactively touch past time entries or invoices.

items.text: Tax Return Delivery: client approval step
items.desc: Firms can now require a client to explicitly confirm they've reviewed a tax return before signing it, instead of treating the signature itself as the only proof of review — including the full client mobile app experience for approving, requesting changes, and tracking status. Fully released after several weeks in Beta.

items.text: Print and download proposals that are still in draft
items.desc: Firms can now print or download a proposal before sending it — handy for an internal review or a sign-off round — instead of having to send it (and notify the client) just to get a PDF. A grey DRAFT stamp marks it clearly as not yet final.

items.text: Filter the Recurring invoices list
items.desc: The Recurring invoices list now has real filters — status, payment collection method, whether a payment method is on file, amount, frequency and more — so firms can find stalled or attention-needed schedules without opening each one individually.

items.text: Automatically update a job's due date
items.desc: Firm Admins can now set a rule so a job's due date updates automatically when it enters a specific pipeline stage or custom status — instead of updating deadlines by hand or reconfiguring the automation every year.

items.text: Inbox+ shows your real notification count
items.desc: The Inbox+ sidebar badge used to cap out at "99+," hiding how many notifications were actually waiting for a firm with a large backlog. It now shows the exact total.

items.text: Desktop app: stay signed in for up to 30 days
items.desc: On a trusted, single-user machine, firms can now turn on a setting that skips re-entering email, password and 2FA after a Windows restart, for up to 30 days at a time — instead of logging back in every time the computer restarts.

items.text: Desktop app can auto-launch on Windows startup
items.desc: Firms who use the Desktop app every day can now have it launch automatically when their computer starts, instead of opening it by hand each time.

items.text: Faster /app/contacts page load
items.desc: The Contacts page should load noticeably faster now, thanks to a round of performance fixes targeting the slowest parts of the page.

items.text: A prebuilt Billing Monitor dashboard
items.desc: A ready-made dashboard for reviewing cash received, posted revenue, and what clients still owe — built for firm owners who currently export payments and AR to Excel to get this picture.

items.text: TRD: choose where the invoice sits in the flow
items.desc: Firms that don't lock documents to an invoice would be able to choose where the invoice shows up in a Tax Return Delivery — before the client views it, after the intro, or right before signing — instead of the current fixed placement that blocks the rest of the flow until it's paid.

items.text: TRD: a clearer first-time setup screen
items.desc: Exploring a clearer explanation of what the Tax Return Delivery flow does during first-time setup, so new users understand it and complete their first delivery instead of abandoning at an empty screen.

items.text: Bulk-create checklists from clients' existing documents
items.desc: Instead of building each client's document checklist by hand, this would generate checklists in bulk straight from documents clients have already uploaded.

items.text: Bulk-create checklists from a CSV
items.desc: Firms with a lot of clients to onboard at once would be able to generate document checklists for all of them in bulk from a CSV file, instead of one account at a time.

items.text: Desktop app: more reliable Drive syncing
items.desc: Ongoing work to make the Desktop app's Drive syncing more trustworthy, with clearer status and error messages when a sync fails instead of files just going missing quietly.

items.text: Desktop app: keeping up with high-volume tax prep firms
items.desc: Speed and bulk-upload improvements aimed at firms that process a high volume of returns, so the Desktop app doesn't slow them down during peak season.

items.text: Roll a checklist forward into the new season
items.desc: Carrying a client's prior-season checklist into the new season instead of losing all that context and rebuilding it from zero every year.

items.text: More than one checklist per client
items.desc: Today a new checklist overwrites the old one. This would let a firm keep several checklists per client at once — for example, one per tax type.

items.text: Affirm or Klarna as a pay-over-time option
items.desc: Exploring adding a Buy Now, Pay Later option like Affirm or Klarna to TaxDome Payments, to make it easier for clients to pay larger invoices.

items.text: Fixed: creating a Tax Return Delivery could fail with a 404
items.desc: Trying to prepare a Tax Return Delivery from a document could fail outright with a 404 error instead of creating the return. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: a proposal saved as a draft before the client had a signer could never be signed
items.desc: If a proposal was saved as a draft before its client contact had signing rights, the list of eligible signers got permanently locked in as empty — so even after the client later got login and signing rights, they could never actually sign it. Fixed so the signer list rebuilds correctly.

items.text: Fixed: signed scanned documents could render blank except for the signature stamps
items.desc: Scanned e-file authorization forms (like Form 8879) could come back showing nothing but the signature stamps after a client signed — the actual scanned content disappeared from view, even though the underlying file was intact. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: relative date shortcodes in scheduled emails resolved to the wrong period
items.desc: A scheduled email using a shortcode like "Last month" or "Last day" resolved that date at the moment the email was scheduled, not when it actually sent — so a report or reminder could reference the wrong period entirely. Fixed to resolve at send time.

items.text: Fixed: a signature request could go missing after an inactive contact was later activated
items.desc: If a document was sent for signature to a contact who hadn't yet been activated, and that contact was activated afterward, the signature request never appeared in their to-do list — leaving them with no way to sign except through the original email. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: a scheduled invoice with "pay with credits" could lose its schedule and settle early
items.desc: Editing a scheduled invoice that had "pay with credits" turned on could drop its future schedule entirely and immediately settle available credits against it, instead of waiting for its intended date. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: moving a document into a Private folder could silently unlink it from its job
items.desc: Moving a document into a Private folder within the same client account could quietly disconnect it from the job and tasks it was linked to, with no warning. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: a paid invoice's line items could show Tax = $0.00 while the invoice total stayed correct
items.desc: Once an invoice with tax on a service line item was marked or recorded as Paid, that line's Tax column could reset to $0.00 in the invoice details view, even though the invoice's overall Total Tax stayed accurate. Fixed.

poll.label: Tax Return Delivery: client approval step

mystery: The Tax Return Delivery client approval step spent exactly 18 days in Beta — from Aug 31 to Sep 17 — before graduating to full release this week.
